eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent cloud cover, widespread thunderstorms, and a cool northerly flow have suppressed daytime heating across Mexico City today, keeping maximum temperatures well below the August climatological average of 23–24 °C. Official forecasts from the Servicio Meteorológico Nacional and international models converge on afternoon readings between 18 °C and 20 °C, with the highest values most likely occurring under brief breaks in the overcast skies around 14–16 local time. The city’s high elevation and urban heat-island effects introduce modest variability among observing sites, while heavy rainfall further limits solar insolation. Traders therefore assign the greatest implied probabilities to 19 °C and 20 °C, reflecting the narrow but still uncertain range between model consensus and real-time observational updates expected before market resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent forecasts for Chongqing on August 26 converge on a daily maximum of 36–38 °C, with model outputs and agency guidance clustered in that narrow band.** This produces the tightest market pricing around 37 °C (26.5 %) and 38 °C (30.5 %), followed by 39 °C (21 %), while lower (36 °C, 12 %) and higher (40 °C+, <7 % combined) outcomes receive less weight.

Chongqing’s Sichuan Basin location favors strong daytime heating under mostly clear or partly cloudy skies: weak pressure gradients produce light easterly or variable winds, limiting mixing, while high solar insolation in late August drives rapid temperature rise after sunrise. Dew points near 24–26 °C add humidity but do not directly alter the dry-bulb maximum that the market resolves on. Minor differences among leading outcomes stem from small variations in forecast cloud cover, timing of any scattered afternoon showers, and resolution of the precise peak hour—factors that numerical models still disagree on by 1–2 °C this far out.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent South African Weather Service and international model guidance indicate a high-pressure ridge promoting mostly clear to partly cloudy conditions over Cape Town on August 26, favoring diurnal heating that supports a maximum near 20–22 °C under light southerly flow. Trader consensus, reflected in the broad distribution peaking at 25 °C, incorporates uncertainty from potential model divergence on wind shifts or cloud timing that could add 2–4 °C. Key variables include the strength and position of the subtropical high, which modulates northerly advection of warmer air, versus any residual cold-front influence that might enhance mixing and cap temperatures near 23 °C or below. Historical August climatology shows highs averaging 17–19 °C, so any verification above 24 °C would require stronger-than-expected ridging and reduced marine layer influence. Updated model runs and official briefings through August 25 remain the primary near-term catalysts likely to shift implied probabilities.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rpll

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: The closely matched market odds between 31°C and 32°C reflect the southwest monsoon (habagat) currently dominating western Luzon, including Manila, with widespread cloud cover, scattered thunderstorms, and high humidity expected to moderate peak heating on August 26. Official PAGASA guidance points to daily highs near 30–31°C amid overcast conditions, while model consensus from sources like AccuWeather and TimeandDate indicates potential for brief clearing that could allow readings to reach 32°C if convective activity remains limited. Nearby Typhoon Obet (Saudel) east of northern Luzon is enhancing regional moisture and rainfall without direct landfall impacts, keeping maximum temperatures aligned with typical August baselines of 29–32°C. Updated PAGASA and NHC-equivalent briefings over the next 48 hours will be key for any late adjustments to steering patterns or intensity.
